body.en: *Viruses* are not included in the five kingdoms. They are obligate parasites made of protein and genetic material, which is either RNA or DNA, never both. D.J. Ivanowsky found that tobacco mosaic disease was caused by something smaller than bacteria; M.W. Beijerinck called it "contagium vivum fluidum"; W.M. Stanley showed that viruses can be crystallised. The protein coat is the capsid, made of capsomeres. Plant viruses usually have single-stranded RNA, and bacteriophages usually double-stranded DNA.
body.kn: ವೈರಸ್‌ಗಳು ಐದು ಸಾಮ್ರಾಜ್ಯಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಸೇರಿಲ್ಲ. ಅವು ಪ್ರೋಟೀನ್ ಮತ್ತು RNA ಅಥವಾ DNA ಯಿಂದಾದ ಕಡ್ಡಾಯ ಪರಾವಲಂಬಿಗಳು. ಬೈಜರಿಂಕ್ "ಕಂಟೇಜಿಯಂ ವೈವಮ್ ಫ್ಲೂಯಿಡಮ್" ಎಂದರು; ಸ್ಟಾನ್ಲಿ ಹರಳಾಗಿಸಿದರು. ಪ್ರೋಟೀನ್ ಹೊದಿಕೆ ಕ್ಯಾಪ್ಸಿಡ್.

title.en: On the board: Viruses, viroids, prions and lichens

say.en: A virus is just a protein coat around its genetic material.
The coat is the capsid made of capsomeres; inside is RNA or DNA, never both.
Ivanowsky found it, Beijerinck named it contagium vivum fluidum, Stanley crystallised it.
Viroids are naked RNA; prions are misfolded proteins.
A lichen is an alga and a fungus living together; it is a sign of clean air.
The alga, the phycobiont, makes food; the fungus, the mycobiont, gives shelter and water.

body.en: *Viroids*, discovered by T.O. Diener in 1971, are free RNA without a protein coat; they cause potato spindle tuber disease. body.en: *Lichens* are symbiotic associations of algae and fungi. The algal partner, the phycobiont, makes food; the fungal partner, the mycobiont, gives shelter and absorbs water and minerals. Lichens do not grow in polluted areas, so they are good indicators of air pollution.

say.en: Plantae: chlorophyll-bearing eukaryotes; Animalia: heterotrophic, wall-less multicellular eukaryotes.
Viruses are nucleoproteins; obligate parasites; DNA or RNA inside a capsid.
Viroids are free RNA (Diener, 1971); prions are misfolded proteins (BSE, CJD).
Lichens = alga (phycobiont) + fungus (mycobiont); sensitive to pollution.

problem.en: A plant disease agent passes through bacterial filters, has RNA, and has no protein coat at all. Is it a virus, a viroid or a prion? Give a reason.

steps.en: A prion is a protein with no nucleic acid, so it cannot be a prion.
A virus always has a protein coat (capsid) around its nucleic acid.
Free RNA without a protein coat is a viroid, like the agent of potato spindle tuber disease.

answer.en: A viroid, because it is naked RNA with no protein coat

narration.en: Recap. Viruses: nucleoprotein, RNA or DNA, obligate parasites. Viroids are naked RNA; prions are misfolded proteins. Lichens: phycobiont plus mycobiont; pollution indicators.
narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ವೈರಸ್: ನ್ಯೂಕ್ಲಿಯೋಪ್ರೋಟೀನ್, RNA ಅಥವಾ DNA, ಕಡ್ಡಾಯ ಪರಾವಲಂಬಿ. ವೈರಾಯ್ಡ್ ಬೆತ್ತಲೆ RNA; ಪ್ರಿಯಾನ್ ತಪ್ಪಾಗಿ ಮಡಚಿದ ಪ್ರೋಟೀನ್. ಕಲ್ಲುಹೂವು: ಫೈಕೋಬಯಾಂಟ್ + ಮೈಕೋಬಯಾಂಟ್; ಮಾಲಿನ್ಯ ಸೂಚಕ.

say.en: Let us recall the key ideas. Viruses: nucleoprotein, RNA or DNA, obligate parasites.
say.kn: ಮುಖ್ಯ ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳೋಣ. ವೈರಸ್: ನ್ಯೂಕ್ಲಿಯೋಪ್ರೋಟೀನ್, RNA ಅಥವಾ DNA, ಕಡ್ಡಾಯ ಪರಾವಲಂಬಿ.
